scope: Assigned items only; read-only local snapshots, rendered HTML, receipts, and screenshot tiles.

findings.symptom: The title says “(pi squared over 6)n” as literal prose/ASCII formula; it is not typeset like the same value in the statement and proof.
findings.suggested_repair: Set the formula in the title with math delimiters, e.g. $(\pi^2/6)n$, or use a prose title that avoids formula notation.

findings.symptom: The title displays “pi(x), theta(x), and psi(x)” as literal ASCII function names while the body typesets these symbols.
findings.suggested_repair: Typeset the functions in the title, e.g. $\pi(x)$, $\theta(x)$, and $\psi(x)$.

findings.symptom: The title displays “Q(zeta_7)” literally instead of the number field notation rendered in the body.
The title displays “Q(sqrt 5)” literally while the body uses a typeset quadratic field expression.
The title writes “log x plus O(1)” in literal ASCII words, unlike the typeset asymptotic formula in the statement.
findings.suggested_repair: Typeset the asymptotic phrase, e.g. $\log x+O(1)$, or recast the title in non-formula prose.

diagram_candidates_note: No source-supported diagram candidate identified. The audited items state maps, relations, arithmetic identities, classifications, and general theorem arguments algebraically; a diagram would add no necessary labels, domain/codomain data, orientation, signs, or combinatorics. No gratuitous diagram requested.

rejected_renderer_intent_observations.symptom: Inline item references render as full-width block links, so “By” and the linked title occupy separate lines. Root confirmed this is intentional MathMarkdown behavior; the observed line break is therefore not a rendering defect.
rejected_renderer_intent_observations.suggested_repair: Render inline `[[item-id]]` references as inline anchors, reserving block display for references that occupy a standalone paragraph.
rejected_renderer_intent_observations.disposition: Rejected as a defect under the renderer-scope decision; retained as a reviewed observation only.
